sections.title: Positioning
sections.summary: Square sells a complete small-business toolkit by industry: restaurants, retail, beauty, health and wellness, home services. The pitch is that one plan runs payments, hardware, booking, online selling and marketing.
keyPoints: Homepage promise: 'Local legend or global icon. Make it big on your block.'
Business-type pages (coffee shops, bars, spas, landscaping and more) each repeat the same suite in that trade's language.
The company page frames Square as built to give every owner an easier way to take credit cards, then grown into a full suite and loans.

sections.title: Products and offerings
sections.summary: Square pairs software with its own hardware and a financial layer, then adds vertical tools on top.

rows: In person (7 ways), online, remote, invoices and Afterpay; Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android
Register $899, Handheld $399, Terminal $299, Stand $149; readers start at $59
Booking site, staff schedules, reminders and Google Calendar sync
Free site builder with customizable themes, shipping, pickup and delivery
Email and text campaigns, automations and CRM tools
Checking and savings accounts; payroll from $35 a month plus $6 per person
Self-service kiosk, order management and restaurant operations
Third-party apps with ratings and free trials

gaps: Loans and Capital were not opened.

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: Per-location monthly plans with a $0 entry and a processing rate that falls as the plan rises, plus a custom plan for large processors. Hardware is sold separately, with monthly financing.
keyPoints: Free is pay-as-you-go: you only pay when you take a payment.
Plus and Premium come with a 30-day free trial; Plus is labelled best value.
Hardware can be financed: the Register is $899 or $44 a month over 24 months.
Square Pro is custom pricing for businesses processing over $250,000 a year, with hardware discounts and onboarding.

rows: POS app, online site, invoicing, booking, banking
Advanced POS features, loyalty, email and text marketing, staff management
24/7 priority support, advanced reporting, no gift card load fees

gaps: Hardware and payroll costs are on separate pages; there is no all-in estimate.

sections.title: Merchandising
sections.summary: A clear, industry-aware ladder: a $0 entry, a best-value middle plan, and a premium tier whose main draw is support. For merchants, Square supplies deep selling and customer-engagement tools.
keyPoints: The pricing page asks 'Tell us about your business' and offers an industry selector, so the plan feature list is tailored.
Processing fees drop with each plan, which ties the monthly price to the merchant's own volume.
Plans, hardware and add-ons cross-sell each other: the plan page links to Payroll, Hardware and Banking.
For merchants: customizable e-commerce themes, inventory across locations and channels, a loyalty program, email and text marketing, Google Reviews tools and shipping discounts.
The App Marketplace lists third-party apps with ratings and 7 or 14-day free trials.

sections.title: Technical platform
sections.summary: A dedicated developer site with APIs and SDKs across the commerce stack, a new Reporting API in beta, and an app marketplace.
keyPoints: APIs named on the developer page include Bookings, Customers, Orders, Catalog, ListPayments and Terminal, plus a Mobile Payments SDK.
A Reporting API (Beta) is advertised as a new way to access all of a business's data.
The App Marketplace has staff picks, most-popular and highest-rated lists, and add-ons for Square Online.
gaps: API reference, rate limits and webhooks were not read.

sections.title: Design
sections.summary: A polished, consumer-grade look: full-bleed photography, very large display type and pill buttons, anchored by one blue. Developer pages switch to a dark theme with smaller buttons.
keyPoints: A custom typeface (Square Sans) runs across home, pricing and the developer site; some pages use Cash Sans.
The accent is a single blue (#006aff); buttons are full pills (10000px corners) on pricing and the main site.
The developer site is dark (#121212) with 4.8px button corners, a visible shift from the marketing pages.
Home opens on a full-bleed photograph with a headline across it; the pricing page puts three white plan cards over a dark photograph.
Pages are long: the home page is 10,597px tall.
For merchants: customizable themes for Square Online, plus logo and brand-color invoices.

sections.title: Company presentation
sections.summary: A friendly, inclusive story aimed at owners of every size, backed by a scale number on the signup page.
keyPoints: The Why Square page leads with 'Helping every size of business succeed' and an origin story about card acceptance.
Signup page claims 4 million+ businesses run on Square.
Customer proof appears as industry showcases rather than a dedicated customer-stories page.
gaps: No leadership or investor information in the surveyed pages.

signupPath: 'Sign up' opens app.squareup.com/signup, a real account form titled 'Let's create your account': email, password and locale (United States, English), a consent line for Terms, Privacy Policy and E-Sign Consent, and a 'Create account' button, with a reCAPTCHA notice. One click from the homepage. Nothing was entered.

jtbd_fit.evidence: Each business-type page names the owner's trade and the jobs: take payments, book, sell online, run staff.

capability_visible.evidence: Product pages show features and hardware prices in detail; the admin itself is behind signup.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Three plans with prices and processing rates are published; hardware, payroll and loan costs sit on other pages.

product_breadth.evidence: Hardware, payments, booking, online, marketing, banking and payroll are each explained with a clear job.

platform_depth.evidence: Developer site lists many APIs, SDKs and a beta Reporting API plus an app marketplace; reference docs were not read.

time_to_value.evidence: Capture stops before the product; first-value time was not observed.

friction.evidence: One click from home to a short form: email, password and locale, with a consent line and reCAPTCHA.

trust.evidence: 4 million+ businesses claim on the signup page and industry showcases; fewer named customers than Stripe or Klaviyo.

mobile.evidence: Phone captures exist for home and pricing but were not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: The homepage headline is mood-led but each industry page and the plan page say plainly what you get.

proof_quality.evidence: Scale and 'best value' claims have no source on the page.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: Trials are stated with their length, and the free plan says you pay only on a payment.

cta_logic.evidence: 'Get started' with 'Contact sales' on pages; plan cards each carry a clear action.

company_narrative.evidence: The 'every size of business' story is consistent from the homepage to Why Square to the signup page.

offer_packaging.evidence: Plans per location with fees in a table, an industry selector and a best-value label make the choice easy.

offer_architecture.evidence: $0 entry, 30-day trials, falling processing fees, hardware financing and a custom plan form a deliberate ladder.

merchant_merch_tools.evidence: Themes, cross-channel inventory, loyalty, email and text marketing, Google Reviews tools and shipping discounts are all shown.

visual_craft.evidence: Strong photography and display type, one blue, clear plan cards. The home hero text sits over a busy photograph.

system_coherence.evidence: Pill buttons and white pages on the main site, dark 4.8px-button developer pages, and two typefaces (Square Sans and Cash Sans).

merchant_design_control.evidence: Customizable themes for the online store and branded invoices are shown; no theme builder detail was surveyed.

read.summary: A vertical-first small-business suite with the clearest plan ladder of the survey so far: a $0 entry, per-location pricing, fees that fall as you move up and hardware that can be financed. The signup is a short, real account form.
pros: Pricing table puts monthly price and both processing rates side by side.
An industry selector tailors the plan features to the merchant's trade.
Hardware prices and financing are shown on the page.
Merchants get a wide set of selling and engagement tools in one place.
cons: The homepage headline is mood-led rather than specific.
Developer pages look and behave differently from the marketing site.
Hardware, payroll and banking costs are spread across several pages.
Scale and 'best value' claims are unsourced.
read.howItSells: Sells simplicity and local-business pride: a free start, one plan per location, and tools by trade. Backs it with a visible price list and a large business count.
copy: Show processing rates beside the monthly price in each plan card.
Offer an industry selector on the pricing page.
Finance hardware with a stated monthly figure.
avoid: A mood-led hero headline with no product statement.
Different button shapes between marketing and developer pages.
unknowns: Payroll and banking details beyond the headline price.

hypothesis.statement: Adding an 'all-in estimate' tool that combines plan, hardware and processing for a typical month will raise paid-plan starts among hesitant visitors.
hypothesis.guardrail: Support contacts about fees and early churn
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if conversion rises by a pre-agreed margin over four weeks and fee-related contacts do not rise.

merchandising.summary: A clear, trade-by-trade ladder, the strongest merchandising of the survey so far, with a real merchant toolset behind it.
pros: The Free, Plus and Premium ladder lowers risk at each step.
Processing fees fall as the plan rises, so the plan sells itself to high-volume merchants.
Hardware financing is stated in monthly terms.
cons: No all-in monthly estimate across plan, hardware and processing.
Add-on prices sit on separate pages.

design.summary: Premium consumer-grade design on the main site, with a visible seam where the developer pages begin.
pros: Full-bleed photography and display type make the marketing site feel premium.
One blue accent and pill buttons make actions easy to spot.
cons: The developer site changes theme and button shape.
Home hero text sits over a busy photograph.

claims.text: Join the 4 million+ businesses running with Square.
Only pay when you take a payment.
Square was established to give every business owner an easier way to take credit cards.

focus: signup to accept first payment; hardware selection to cart; eligibility explanation; signup to online store
